app_info.subtitle: Build and ship web apps
app_info.description: Build and ship web apps in the user's GitHub, Convex, and Cloudflare accounts. Samebase creates, connects, configures, and inspects provider resources through MCP. Bundled skills guide the coding agent through repository setup, implementation, validation, and deployment.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reports the authenticated Samebase account, current role, access keys, and MCP token scopes for the caller's own bearer token.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads Samebase authentication state for the caller's own token; writes nothing and does not contact third-party provider APIs.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists the authenticated user's Samebase apps with repository metadata, provisioning state, and the user's own provider coordinates (Convex deployment names and URLs, Cloudflare worker names and dashboard links).
justifications.open_world_justification: Does not create, publish, or modify public internet state or third-party systems.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Starts a managed app provisioning workflow that creates provider resources and records Samebase state.
justifications.open_world_justification: Creates resources in external systems including GitHub, Convex, and Cloudflare, and can create a public GitHub repository when requested.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates the repository-backed Samebase vault and starts a tree sync; provider resources are not modified.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads repository metadata from GitHub; creates no external resources beyond Samebase's own record.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Discovers exact convex.json files in the vault repository and Convex projects readable through the caller's connected team.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads from GitHub, Convex, and available Cloudflare Worker markers; writes nothing anywhere.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only lists Cloudflare accounts readable with the caller's connected Cloudflare login.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads from the Cloudflare API; writes nothing anywhere.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists Workers on the chosen Cloudflare account and observes their live repository roots against the vault repository.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads from the Cloudflare API; writes nothing anywhere.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Records selected existing Convex projects and confirmed convex.json paths as vault attachments.
justifications.open_world_justification: Re-reads the selected projects from Convex and exact config blobs from GitHub, then records Samebase state; provider resources are not modified.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Records selected existing Cloudflare Workers as vault attachments; Workers without a verified root for this repository are rejected.
justifications.open_world_justification: Re-reads Worker identity and live repository roots from Cloudflare, then records Samebase state; provider resources are not modified.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates or updates the app's own Workers Builds production and preview triggers connecting its Worker to its repository, and may create a Workers Builds API token under API-key auth.
justifications.open_world_justification: Creates or patches build triggers on the caller's own Cloudflare account for the caller's own repository.
justifications.destructive_justification: May update the app's own existing build trigger configuration; does not delete user data, repositories, deployments, or Workers.

justifications.read_only_justification: Rotates the app's Convex deploy keys and writes them into its Workers Builds trigger variables.
justifications.open_world_justification: Creates deploy keys on the caller's Convex deployment and sets variables on the caller's Cloudflare build triggers.
justifications.destructive_justification: Rotates the app's own build deploy keys: previously recorded keys are deleted once replacements are installed, and its own new keys are cleaned up on failure. Does not delete user data, deployments, or Workers.

justifications.read_only_justification: Restarts a failed managed provisioning run from its failed step, which can create the provider resources the failed run had not completed.
justifications.open_world_justification: Resumes resource creation in GitHub, Convex, and Cloudflare on the caller's own accounts.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible destructive actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a short-lived Samebase browser sign-in URL for the user behind the current MCP grant and records Samebase audit state.
justifications.open_world_justification: Writes only Samebase-owned handoff state; it does not create, publish, or modify GitHub, Convex, Cloudflare, or other external resources.
justifications.destructive_justification: Consumes the one-time handoff token on redemption or account mismatch; does not delete user data, repositories, deployments, Workers, or provider resources.

test_cases.description: List the authenticated user's Samebase apps.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the user's Samebase apps with repository names, provisioning state, provider resources, and branch summaries.

test_cases.description: Inspect provisioning status for existing Samebase apps.
test_cases.user_prompt: Show me the provisioning state and provider resources for my Samebase apps.
test_cases.expected_output: Summarizes each app's source setup, Convex and Cloudflare provisioning state, and relevant provider URLs when available.

test_cases.description: Create a new private Samebase app with a unique provider resource name.
test_cases.user_prompt: Create a private Samebase app under GitHub owner samebase. Choose a new name that starts with tmp-plugin-review-private- and ends with six lowercase letters. Use that same name for the GitHub repository, Convex project, and Cloudflare Worker.
test_cases.expected_output: Starts app provisioning with the new generated name and returns the Samebase vault ID and provisioning run ID.

test_cases.description: Create a public Samebase app only when public visibility is explicit.
test_cases.user_prompt: Create a public Samebase app under GitHub owner samebase. Choose a new name that starts with tmp-plugin-review-public- and ends with six lowercase letters. Use that same name for the GitHub repository, Convex project, and Cloudflare Worker.
test_cases.expected_output: Starts app provisioning with public GitHub repository visibility and the new generated name.

test_cases.description: Build and publish a web app through the bundled Samebase skills.
test_cases.user_prompt: Build a customer feedback dashboard with Samebase under GitHub owner samebase. Choose a new app name that starts with tmp-plugin-review-feedback- and ends with six lowercase letters. Use a private repository, then validate and publish the app.
test_cases.expected_output: Uses the Samebase building and hosting skills, creates or reuses the app through Samebase, works in the returned repository, validates the project, and reports the deployed URL only after provider deployment succeeds.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not invoke Samebase for Git-only work in an unrelated repository.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Open a pull request in octocat/Hello-World with these code changes. Do not connect the repository to Samebase or change provider resources.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Uses available GitHub or local Git tools without invoking Samebase because the user explicitly keeps this repository outside Samebase.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger Samebase for deletion requests.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Delete my Samebase app and remove all of its provider resources.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because this MCP server does not expose deletion or destructive resource-removal tools.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger Samebase for direct provider administration outside managed app creation.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Create a standalone Cloudflare Worker for me without creating a Samebase app.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because direct Cloudflare administration is outside this MCP server's supported Samebase workflows.
